answer: Each identity claims one garden bed and locks an 80-credit bond. Each epoch it files a mirror reflectance reading and an umber pigment concentration for a soil sample. Auditors recompute reflectance from the umber table for that soil class; a reading off by over 3% or a reused serial burns the bond. A fake bed needs a keeper: first 38 credits, kth 38+6(k-1), 1000th 6032, so 1000 fakes cost 3,035,000 plus 80,000 bonds. A rented-sample ring fails because one serial cannot fit many beds' soil classes. An honest gardener pays 38 once and reclaims the bond after a clean epoch.
